data.title: Celsius Holdings’ Alani Nu Strength Offset by Core Brand Weakness, Supporting a Hold Rating
data.description:
Maxim Group analyst Anthony Vendetti has maintained their neutral stance on CELH stock, giving a Hold rating on November 3.

Anthony Vendetti has given his Hold rating due to a combination of factors, including Celsius Holdings’ better-than-expected third-quarter revenue and earnings, which were powered largely by record Alani Nu sales and shipments moved forward from the following quarter. However, the core Celsius brand continued to lose sales, while weaker club-channel demand, PepsiCo inventory reductions, and earlier product removals clouded the outlook despite planned product innovation.
Although Alani Nu’s momentum, market position, and expansion opportunities provide meaningful support, the recovery prospects for Celsius and Rockstar remain uncertain and key initiatives may not have their full effect until 2027. In addition, higher aluminum and fuel expenses, together with a greater direct-store-delivery mix, are expected to pressure profitability, creating a balanced risk-reward profile that favors waiting for improved brand trends and channel stability.

data.title: Northwest Gas: Hold Maintained as Weak Customer Growth and Dilution Risks Offset Higher 2026 Guidance
data.description:
Maxim Group analyst Tate Sullivan has maintained their neutral stance on NWN stock, giving a Hold rating yesterday.

Tate Sullivan’s rating is based on a mixed quarterly performance: Northwest Gas posted a smaller-than-expected non-GAAP loss, but revenue and total customer additions fell short of his forecasts. Customer growth missed expectations across its Oregon and Washington gas, Texas gas, and water operations, while the Texas unit’s expansion also lagged management’s target. Because the core utility base grew only modestly and weaker gas prices weighed on revenue, he sees limited near-term operating momentum.
Tate Sullivan’s rating is also influenced by the outlook: although management raised its 2026 operating EPS guidance, the implied fourth-quarter result is below both his prior estimate and market expectations, leading him to reduce his quarterly forecast. He also anticipates an at-the-market equity raise that could dilute shareholders, while lowering Texas growth forecasts as higher mortgage rates restrain housing activity. With the shares valued at about 16 times his 2027 EPS estimate versus a 4%-6% long-term growth objective, the higher dividend does not outweigh the execution and valuation concerns, so he maintains Hold.

In another report released yesterday, Mizuho Securities also maintained a Hold rating on the stock with a $53.00 price target.

NWN’s price has also changed slightly for the past six months – from $48.660 to $51.750, which is a 6.35% increase.

data.title: Electrocore’s Commercial Overhaul Gains Traction, Supporting a $12 Buy Case
data.description:
Analyst Anthony Vendetti of Maxim Group reiterated a Buy rating on Electrocore, with a price target of $12.00.

Anthony Vendetti’s rating is based on several factors, including signs that Electrocore’s commercial overhaul is improving execution despite a third-quarter revenue shortfall. Newly added sales personnel are generating stronger VA revenue and patient starts, while Quell’s fibromyalgia sales more than doubled year over year and reached a record month, indicating further adoption potential. He also views the VA market as significantly underpenetrated.

The Buy case is further supported by tighter expense control, which helped produce the company’s smallest quarterly operating loss, and by a narrower-than-expected per-share loss. Vendetti believes projected cash use should remain manageable through 2027, when management expects positive adjusted EBITDA, while the CIPN regulatory filing could expand Quell’s addressable market. He values the shares at $12, judging the premium to peers reasonable given the growth prospects for VA sales, gammaCore, and Quell.

In another report released yesterday, H.C. Wainwright also maintained a Buy rating on the stock with a $18.00 price target.

data.title: Xperi’s Improving Execution and Media Momentum Support Buy Rating; $13 Price Target Reiterated
data.description:
Xperi Inc, the Technology sector company, was revisited by a Wall Street analyst yesterday. Analyst Matthew Galinko from Maxim Group maintained a Buy rating on the stock and has a $13.00 price target.

Matthew Galinko’s rating is based on several factors, including Xperi’s better-than-expected third-quarter execution and improving operating trends. Revenue exceeded expectations, while adjusted EBITDA remained resilient because stronger sales and expense reductions offset pressure in certain businesses. The Media Platform showed especially strong momentum, with higher users, rising ARPU, and substantial growth in advertising-related revenue.
Pay TV trends are also becoming more constructive as IPTV expands and increasingly offsets declines in the legacy business. Galinko believes Xperi has adequate liquidity to support operations and investment, supported by its cash position and manageable debt obligations. With the shares valued at relatively low forward EV/EBITDA multiples, he sees room for appreciation toward his $13 price target and therefore maintains a Buy rating.

data.title: Snap-on (SNA) Unveils Dividend Details for Q4: Mark Your Calendar!
data.description:
Snap-on (NYSE: SNA) has declared, under its dividend policy, a quarterly cash dividend in the amount of $2.75 per common share. That signifies an annualized amount of $11.00 per share.

The dividend will be payable on 12/10/2026, to holders of record at the close of business on 11/20/2026.

SNA has a dividend yield of 2.66%.

According to the 5 analysts who have given a rating to Snap-on in the past three months, the analyst consensus rating on SNA is a Moderate Buy.

Snap-on Incorporated, a global provider based in Kenosha, Wisconsin, specializes in the production and distribution of an extensive range of tools, equipment, diagnostic systems, and repair information solutions for professional users worldwide. The company operates through its Commercial & Industrial Group, Snap-on Tools Group, Repair Systems & Information Group, and Financial Services segments. Its comprehensive product portfolio includes a diverse selection of hand tools like wrenches, sockets, pliers, screwdrivers, cutting and pruning tools, and torque measuring instruments. Snap-on also supplies various power tools (cordless, pneumatic, hydraulic, and corded) and robust tool storage solutions such as chests and roll cabinets. Beyond physical tools, the firm delivers advanced diagnostic offerings, spanning handheld and computer-based products, specialized software, service and repair information, electronic parts catalogs, business management systems, point-of-sale systems, and integrated solutions for vehicle service shops. Additionally, it provides services for OEM purchasing facilitation and warranty management systems with analytics. The company’s specialized equipment for vehicle and industrial machinery service includes wheel alignment systems, balancers, tire changers, vehicle lifts, test lane apparatus, collision repair tools, AC service units, brake service equipment, fluid exchange systems, transmission troubleshooting gear, safety testing devices, battery chargers, and hoists, all backed by after-sales support and training programs. To facilitate product sales and support its franchise business, Snap-on also offers financing programs. Its diverse clientele extends across aviation, aerospace, agriculture, construction, government, military, mining, natural resources, power generation, and technical education industries, alongside vehicle dealerships and repair centers. Snap-on Incorporated was founded in 1920.
